Both legs of the 2026-09-19 cycle independently marked this paragraph as the article's weakest, for different reasons — treat the paragraph as needing one coordinated rewrite, not two. **Verified loci:** L~101 "would *not* be identical to ours" (offset 12715); the concession "is speculative" (13239) immediately followed by "the interactionist framework predicts they exist" (13259); "the zombie meta-problem dissolves" (13633). **The defect:** a philosophical zombie is by definition a *physical* duplicate, and `apex/born-preserving-causal-efficacy` states at L119 that "under corridor-plus-trumping, 'consciousness is a cause' and 'consciousness is epiphenomenal' make no predictively distinct claims at any scale" and at L67 that single-event efficacy "aggregates to **no statistical signature**". On the Map's own account the duplicate's physical trajectory, reports included, is reproducible without consciousness — so the divergence is not merely undetectable, it is absent. Retaining "predicts … but speculative" is confession-without-demotion: the defect is logged and the dependent claim keeps its original strength. **Either** drop "the interactionist framework predicts they exist", **or** convert the section into an explicit statement of the Born-rule statistical-indistinguishability dilemma and cross-link the apex. Adopt that apex's compatible / suggestive / discriminating ladder and label the divergence claim **interface-compatible** at best. **Do not quote the apex as saying "no statistical signature in long runs"** — the reviewer's rendering; "long run(s)" occurs zero times in that file. Length-neutral or trimming; this file is at 2595/3500 with four other open tasks.
  **3/3 CONVERGENCE — confirmed once the 2026-09-19 Gemini leg was collected.** All three outer reviewers this cycle independently marked the **zombie/dissolution paragraph (L101-103)** as the article's weakest passage, each arriving by a different route: ChatGPT via the causal-closure contradiction at L103; Claude via this finding (the Map's own Born-preserving commitment leaves no divergence to detect); and Gemini (`reviews/outer-review-2026-09-19-gemini-2-5-pro.md`, Dimension 3, "Circularity in the Zombie Debunking Threat") via circularity — the article assumes the only escape from overdetermination is a non-physical causal power, and never engages the physicalist **identity** response that the phenomenal state and the physical processing state are one event described under two conceptual schemes.
  **Implication for the fix**: three independent routes to one paragraph means the paragraph itself, not any single sentence in it, is what needs rewriting. Gemini's identity-response point is the only one of the three not already on record and is cheap to absorb: the passage needs a sentence acknowledging that identity theory dissolves the overdetermination worry without dualism, and saying why the Map declines that route.

(b) is the cheapest and preserves every existing URL. Whichever is chosen, re-word the prompt template in the same change so the three services stop being asked for what they cannot fetch. Allen 2022 (*European Journal for Philosophy of Science* 12(2), art. 28, doi 10.1007/s13194-022-00451-3) was read IN FULL on 2026-10-22 via its PhilSci-Archive manuscript and the published Springer HTML (Wayback). Twenty quotes were verified, with a negative control. Her argument: in any powers ontology, explicitly including identity-thesis powerful qualities, zombie conceivability yields zombie possibility only if physical powers produce phenomenal properties by "a contingent form of emergence which mimics the behaviour of categorical properties". She calls that "fairly implausible and unlikely". Without independent reasons she calls such an ontology "question-begging since it seems entirely motivated by the desire to make physicalism a contingent doctrine and to provide an ontology in which the conceivability argument applies". Supervenient and causal emergence hold with nomological necessity on a powers view, so they do not restore zombies. Non-physical phenomenal powers, epiphenomenal or causally efficacious, get her pure-powers treatment, and a world where the physical does not produce the phenomenal "is one where dualism is true", not a starting point for the argument. She notes that her argument does not make powers theories inconsistent with dualism, so DUALISM IS NOT REFUTED. The issue is circularity in the Map's own reasoning. WHY IT BEARS ON THE MAP: the Map holds identity-thesis powerful qualities (`concepts/causal-powers` L41, L75). It picks contingent governing laws over dispositional essentialism because a zombie world is conceivable (causal-powers L79; `topics/consciousness-and-the-metaphysics-of-laws-and-dispositions` L96-L102, L126, L142). So the ontology that keeps zombie worlds possible is selected by appeal to zombie conceivability, and the zombie argument is then counted toward dualism. OPTIONS: (a) give independent reasons for contingent psychophysical production, e.g. the legislation or quantum-anchor arguments at laws-page L84-L86 and L140-L146, and engage Allen on the laws page; (b) concede on causal-powers and the laws page that the governing-laws choice presupposes zombie contingency, so the zombie premise cannot count as independent support inside the Map's own ontology (matches `concepts/modal-epistemology` L121: zombie possibility "no longer counts as independent evidence" on the rival routes); (c) check whether "different laws are metaphysically possible with the same properties" (causal-powers L59) is coherent with the identity thesis, which Allen takes to fix causal role essentially. SECONDARY: Allen groups powerful qualities with Russellian monism, a rival the Map rejects, which would push the zombie argument's conclusion into Chalmers 2010's Russellian-monism disjunct. Whatever is decided, update modal-epistemology L127, which marks the question open, and the [P-D1](/positions/arguments-for-dualism/#p-d1) register entry if its premise's standing changes. Do NOT let a fork resolve this in prose.

EDIT (1): insert a NEW paragraph between L51 and L53, as two bold-lead arguments in the page's existing style (adapt wording): "**The conceivability criterion proves too much.** Galileo's own test was conceivability: he could not conceive a body without bounds, shape, place and motion, but felt no such necessity to conceive it as white or red ([galilean-exclusion](/concepts/galilean-exclusion/); Galilei 1623/1957). Berkeley turned the test around: no one can frame the idea of an extended, moving body without giving it some colour or other sensible quality, so by the same test extension is wherever colour is (Berkeley 1710, *Principles* §10). Applied evenly, it claims colour's structure too, since colour spaces and unique-hue data are mathematised, and it leaves out only the felt quality ([structure is tractable; quality is not](/topics/colour-ontology-and-the-secondary-quality-residue/#structure)). ### ✓ 2026-10-30: Neutrality repairs in `voids/molyneux-void`: Green 2024 is cited as the warrant for a dualism-neutrality he does not address (L45, L95), and §What AI Might See (L89) has an unmarked structure/experience premise and two overclaims
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/voids/molyneux-void.md
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review Priority 3 (Medium-High; calibration). The page's NEUTRALITY verdict is correct and must stay. These edits repair its warrant and remove one breach. (A) GREEN. The Green (2024) abstract (OpenAlex, verbatim) says the all-possible-perceivers question "cannot be used to adjudicate debates about whether the phenomenal character of perceptual experience is primarily determined 'externally' by the worldly properties we perceive, or 'internally' by physiological or functional properties of our brains". That is the internalism/externalism dispute about phenomenal character, both of whose standard positions are physicalist; dualism is not a party to it. Yet L45 (the lead) and L95 place Green beside the dualism-neutrality claim as if he warranted it. L45 OLD: `The void is epistemic and neutral between dualism and physicalism. E. J. Green (2024) argues that even the question's most general version cannot decide whether phenomenal character is fixed by the world or by the brain.` NEW: `The void is epistemic and neutral between dualism and physicalism, since a dualist and a physicalist describe the same blank. E. J. Green (2024) reaches a parallel verdict on a neighbouring dispute: even the question's most general version, he argues, cannot decide whether phenomenal character is fixed by the world or by the brain.` (+13). PRONOUN: the next sentence, `Its value to the Map is calibration.`, would then attach "Its" to Green's "most general version". Change it to `The void's value to the Map is calibration.` (+1). L95: immediately after the Green quotation, which ends `or 'internally' by physiological or functional properties of our brains."`, INSERT `That dispute is not the dualism dispute, so Green supplies a parallel to the neutrality claimed here, not its premise.` (+19). Keep the next sentence ("No author cited here argues from the Molyneux record to dualism ...") as the real warrant. (B) L89, three problems. (i) Unmarked premise. OLD: `But alignment is a third-person structural fact, and whether aligned encoders yield one shape-experience or two, if any, is the seam face's question.` This assumes structure can leave experience open, which functionalists deny. The research note's §What AI Might See marked the same point "a dualist interpretation, not a finding", and the article dropped the marker. NEW: `Alignment is a third-person structural fact. On views on which structure can leave experience open, whether aligned encoders yield one shape-experience or two, if any, is the seam face's question; a functionalist counts the alignment as the answer.` (+12). (ii) The claim `with neither human confound` is too quick. INSERT after the sentence ending `found no such study under the Molyneux label.`: `Whatever puts the two spaces in correspondence, though, is paired training, which is touch teaching sight again, structural matching, which is Clarke's inference in machine form, or a shared format built in by design.` (+33). (iii) OLD: `In a machine the join is open to outside inspection. In a human it is open from neither side, closed to introspection by habit and to experiment by the purity paradox (see [[non-human-minds-as-void-explorers]]).` This overclaims. The purity paradox closes the DEVELOPMENTAL question (given or acquired), not the structural one. fMRI shows haptic object-selective voxels overlapping the visual lateral occipital complex, which the authors suggest "may constitute a multimodal object-related network" (Amedi, Malach, Hendler, Peled & Zohary 2001; verified by Crossref and Europe PMC; abstract read, full text not). NEW: `In a machine both the join's structure and its history are open to outside inspection. In a human the history is closed to introspection by habit and to experiment by the purity paradox, while the mature structure is partly open: haptic shape activates part of the visual lateral occipital complex, which Amedi and colleagues (2001) suggest may be a multimodal object network (see [[non-human-minds-as-void-explorers]]).` (+25). Add the reference in alphabetical position (first) and renumber the list: `Amedi, A., Malach, R., Hendler, T., Peled, S., & Zohary, E. (2001). Visuo-haptic object-related activation in the ventral visual pathway. *Nature Neuroscience*, 4(3), 324–330. https://doi.org/10.1038/85201` (~+20). Task total ~+120; if headroom is short, drop (ii) first. ChatGPT (§1/§3/§4): "the main weakness is modal overreach... a physicalist can accept that 'minimal consciousness' is hard to locate without conceding irreducibility," and the article "uses the worldview to close questions it should leave open." Concretely the convergent edits are: separate (E) from (M1)/(M2) and either retreat to (E) or supply the missing argument; soften/delete the "purely physical phenomenon would have a discoverable minimum" sentence (Φ itself grades continuously to zero, as Claude notes); and downgrade "the void exists precisely because consciousness is causally efficacious / the bidirectional tenet in miniature" to an analogy, since intra-mental attentional modulation is not the mind→matter bidirectional interaction the tenet asserts (Claude). Original ChatGPT note follows. From outer review 2026-06-02 (ChatGPT 5.5 Pro), findings §1, §3, §4 and improvement items 1, 6, 7, 8. The reviewer's substantive (non-citation) critique: the article slides from a defensible claim ("minimal consciousness cannot be *directly introspected/attended/remembered/reported* without enrichment") to an over-strong one ("cannot be investigated at all" / "permanently beyond examination" in every sense), and twice uses the dualist worldview to close questions it should leave open — the "a purely physical phenomenon *would have* a discoverable minimum" sentence (line 95) and "the void exists *precisely because* consciousness is causally efficacious" (line 97). Apply the [direct-refutation-discipline](/project/direct-refutation-discipline/) remit. Identify what kind of engagement the issue calls for: showing the opponent's position is defective on its own terms, naming an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards, or honestly marking the framework-boundary disagreement. Here the right move is mostly the second/third: a physicalist can grant fuzzy/scale-relative/operational thresholds without conceding irreducibility, so the "would have a discoverable minimum" inference is an unearned foundational move; reframe it as "some physicalist theories predict operational thresholds, others predict continua/vagueness/multidimensional boundaries; the absence of a clean lower edge underdetermines the metaphysics," and frame dualism as ONE interpretation the void is consistent with, not the explanation it licenses. Apply the corresponding reply mode in natural journal-quality prose — see [the writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/)'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section. Do NOT expose mode labels in the article body; the classification belongs in the changelog entry, not the article. Concrete edits: (a) add a "Direct vs Indirect Access" distinction so the void is explicitly about *direct phenomenal capture*, not all scientific constraint (no-report paradigms, anaesthesia transition data, animal-consciousness and neural-complexity measures place indirect, underdetermined constraints — "not nothing"); (b) add a short "What Would Challenge This View?" section mirroring the structure already in [minimal-consciousness](/concepts/minimal-consciousness/) (which the reviewer notes is better calibrated than this void article); (c) soften lines 95 and 97 per above. Honour [evidential-status-discipline](/project/evidential-status-discipline/). Length: 1180w on disk, ample headroom — modest growth fine. If an in-framework refutation is attempted and fails, state in natural prose that the disagreement is closer to bedrock than first appeared.

### P2: agentic-social topic-dedup has saturated — the selector pool has collapsed to a tiny empty-topics residue
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: .claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py
- **Status**: blocked (diverted from Active by the cycle driver 2026-07-28 — the notes say "operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally" and list five mutually exclusive options; the loop would have executed it as a refine-draft and picked one. Not an outage: posting works, URL-fallback degrades gracefully.)
- **Notes**: FOUND by the run-11910 `/agentic-social` fork after the driver asked it to investigate a fourth consecutive empty-`topics` selection; **independently driver-reproduced against live state**. **THE MECHANISM** is at `agentic_social_api.py:456`: `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` — an article whose `topics` frontmatter is **empty** short-circuits the overlap check and therefore *can never be filtered out*, while every article that HAS topics is tested against a ban set that now holds **221 topics accumulated from 154 recent posts**. **DRIVER-VERIFIED NUMBERS (live, run 11910)**: 784 candidate articles scanned; a faithful replay of the filter leaves **14 survivors, 12 of them empty-topics (86%)** against an empty-topics base rate of ~9% (71 of 810 articles carrying a `topics` field). The fork's own instrumented count, which also applies the index-page/sidecar guards the driver's cruder replay let through, put the survivor count at **1**. Both figures describe a collapsed pool; the 86%-vs-9% over-representation is the robust signal, and four consecutive empty-topics picks at random would be ~2e-5. **SELF-REINFORCING**: each empty-topics post contributes zero topics back to the ban set, so the set never ages out through variety, and `mark-posted` is legitimately called without `--topics` (correct behaviour — inventing topics would corrupt dedup — but it means topic-level dedup now receives no signal at all). **THE FAILURE MODE IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN THE CODE** at lines 373-402, which anticipates it almost exactly ("once the 7-day topic-dedup filter empties the real-article pool… they become the sole primary-loop survivor and the selector returns them forever") and adds guards for `_`-prefixed files, `stem == parent.name`, `-index`/`-articles` suffixes, and an explicit `social_eligible: false` opt-out. **Those guards treat the symptom** (off-voice index pages reaching the network) **rather than the cause** (topic-dedup saturating). There is a URL-only fallback at :466 when `available` is empty, so this degrades rather than hard-fails — which is why it has gone unnoticed. **OPTIONS — operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally**: (a) expire the topic ban list on a much shorter window than the 7-day URL window (a few days of topics, not 154 posts' worth) — probably the smallest correct fix; (b) cap the ban-set size, evicting oldest first; (c) require overlap above a threshold (e.g. ≥2 shared topics, or a Jaccard floor) rather than rejecting on any single shared topic — note many articles share one broad topic like `consciousness`, which is likely what saturates the set; (d) backfill `topics` frontmatter on the ~71 bare articles, which fixes the short-circuit asymmetry but not the saturation; (e) make the empty-topics case explicit rather than implicit — an article with no topics should arguably be *ineligible* or *neutral*, not *always-eligible*. **DO NOT** simply delete the ban list or widen it to zero days — 7-day URL dedup alone would allow near-immediate thematic repetition, which is what topic dedup exists to prevent. Posting continues to work correctly in the meantime; this is a content-variety defect, not an outage.
  📏 **MEASUREMENT-ONLY ANNOTATION BY /replenish-queue 2026-08-19 00:45Z — STATUS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, still blocked, still the operator's design call. Nothing here unblocks it.** Posting a fresh measurement because a P3 task elsewhere in the queue was citing this entry as evidence of a live failure mode, and the condition it describes no longer reproduces. Calling `get_published_articles()` directly from `agentic_social_api.py` returns a candidate pool of **676 articles of which ZERO have an empty `topics:` list** — the "tiny empty-topics residue" in this entry's title is now empty in the other direction. Three guards added since 2026-07-28 account for it, and the module's own comments narrate their history: the `stem == parent` section-index skip, the `stem.endswith(("-index", "-articles"))` skip, and the `social_eligible: false` opt-out honoured at L432-436. Directory scope does the rest — `CONTENT_DIRS` (L49-53) is only `concepts`, `topics`, `apex`, so the 11 empty-topics files that live under `voids/` and `positions/` were never candidates at all. **Option (d) in the list above — backfill `topics` on the bare articles — is therefore no longer load-bearing for this defect**; it survives only as cosmetic metadata hygiene and is tracked separately at P3. Options (a), (b), (c) and (e) concern ban-set saturation, which this measurement does **not** speak to and which may well still be live. **A human should decide whether that residual saturation question keeps this entry open or closes it.**
- **Source**: driver-found + fork-investigated, /agentic-social run 11910
- **Generated**: 2026-07-28

### Durable fix (NEEDS DEV — not loop-pickable): sync.py must delete orphaned hugo/content files on archive
- **Type**: operator/dev (code change) — do NOT pick as refine-draft; this is a `scripts/sync.py` / `tools/sync/converter.py` change for the operator.
- **Notes**: Root cause of the recurring coalesce-stale-hugo-duplicate-urls / archival_link_rot bug. When an article is archived/coalesced its obsidian source moves to `archive/<sec>/` (which syncs to `hugo/content/archive/<sec>/`), but sync NEVER deletes the original git-tracked `hugo/content/<sec>/<slug>.md`. That orphan keeps serving the full, un-flagged, STALE body at the original URL and shadows the Netlify 301 in `_redirects` (a non-forced redirect loses to a matching static file). **BULK CLEANUP DONE 2026-06-22 (this cycle, commit via auto(refine-draft)):** deleted 317 verified-safe orphans — 160 topics / 58 concepts / 97 voids, plus the 2 ChatGPT-flagged pages (evidential-weight-of-voids, causal-delegation). Every one had a `_redirects` 301 whose target resolves to a LIVE obsidian page (verified 315/315 redirect-present + 0/315 dead-target; a clean `rm -rf public && hugo` build confirmed the deleted URLs are absent (→ 301) while every replacement page still builds; re-sync does not recreate the orphans). **DURABLE FIX still needed:** make sync delete any `hugo/content/<sec>/<slug>.md` whose `obsidian/<sec>/<slug>.md` source no longer exists (it was archived/deleted), GATED on a `_redirects` rule existing for that URL so it can never create a 404. Until shipped, every future `/archive` or `/coalesce` re-introduces one stale duplicate (cf. the 2026-06-14 single-file precedent: the quantum-measurement-interpretations-beyond-mwi removal task).

- **Notes**: **This is the reviewer's improvements #18 and #19, and unlike most methodology proposals from outer reviewers it arrives with a verified failure to point at.** ⚠️ **The concrete defects are already minted as executable tasks (one P1 on `topics/psychedelics-and-the-filter-model`, one P2 on `project/calibration-audit-triple` L495) — this entry is the *policy* question only. Do not duplicate those fixes here.** **The evidence.** The 2026-08-27 deep review of `topics/psychedelics-and-the-filter-model` recorded, in its Citation Web-Verify section (L53 of `reviews/deep-review-2026-08-27-psychedelics-and-the-filter-model.md`): "The remaining 23 entries are unchanged since the 2026-06-03 full publisher-of-record ledger (re-confirmed 2026-06-19 and 2026-07-07); that ledger stands." Under that rule an entry is owed re-verification only if it *changed*. Two entries in that unchanged set are phantoms, verified as such during this review's processing: reference 23 ("Timmermann, C. et al. (2024). DMT alters cortical travelling waves…", no such publication; the real paper is Irrmischer et al. 2026, *J. Neurosci.* 46(2):e0344252025) and reference 9 ("Hameroff, S. (2024) … Cambridge University Press", where the volume is Gao ed., **Oxford**, **2022** and the chapter title does not exist). Both were present on 2026-06-03 and therefore inherited, unchecked, through **four** passes. The same section's L47 shows the deep review *did* touch Timmermann, Mason and Lebedev — but only to trim **recitation redundancy**, never to check what the sources say. A third instance sits at `project/calibration-audit-triple.md` L495, inside the audit specification's own worked exhibit. **The policy question for the operator.** The inheritance rule is what makes the ledger affordable; removing it makes every deep review re-verify ~24 entries. Three options, in ascending cost: **(a)** keep inheritance but make it *tuple-scoped* — an unchanged entry is still owed a one-shot existence check of the (author, year, title, container, volume/pages, DOI) tuple against Crossref, which is cheap and would have caught both phantoms, while the expensive part (does the source support the claim?) stays owed only on change. **(b)** Additionally require, on any entry whose *body claim* is edited — as L47's recitation trim did — that the claim be re-checked against the abstract even if the reference entry itself is untouched; this is the seam that let an editorially-touched citation keep an unverified claim. **(c)** The reviewer's fuller #19: a literature-drift gate for fast-moving empirical pages, searching from the date of the last full empirical audit forward and forbidding ledger inheritance outright on such pages. Note the Map already runs a weekly `literature-drift-review` (Audit One of the triple), so (c) may be partly built — **check what that skill already covers before commissioning new machinery**, and note it audits one article per run, which is a different cadence from a per-pass gate. **Caution against over-reading**: the reviewer's own framing of the Map's review record is partly its own reconstruction, and several 2026 papers it cites are unverified aggregator chips (see the review file's `## Verification Notes`). The *ledger-inheritance* finding stands on this repo's own record, independently of anything the reviewer got right about the literature. **Related open entries** — read before ratifying, they may compose or conflict: `NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-09-02` on binding status changes, and `NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-08-06` on gates-vs-lenses (the same "does this become a blocking gate?" question, previously answered conservatively). **⚠️ CONVERGENCE 2026-09-07 — a second, independent reviewer now names this same policy defect.** The Claude Opus 5 leg of the *same* cycle (`reviews/outer-review-2026-09-06-claude-opus-5.md`, site-wide item #5) reached the ledger-inheritance finding without seeing the ChatGPT leg, and independently re-derived the Reference 23 chimera and the Lebedev misattribution that evidence it — so this is genuine corroboration, not one reviewer's hobby-horse, and it raises the case for ratifying rather than deferring. **Two formulations from that leg are worth carrying into the decision, because they sharpen option (a):** (i) verify the citation **as a tuple** — (author, year, title, container, volume/pages, DOI) checked *together* rather than field-by-field, on the reasoning that Reference 23 was a title-from-paper-A + venue-and-finding-from-paper-B fusion in which **every field was individually plausible** and only the combination was false, so a field-by-field check cannot catch this class; and (ii) state the inheritance bar directly — **a review pass may not inherit a previous pass's verification without re-checking the raw record** — with the specific diagnostic that *any citation whose components trace to two different DOIs is a hard fail*. That reviewer also names the structural reason the pipeline is prone to it: plausible metadata assembled from adjacent sources, then a Claude-on-Claude review loop that re-ratifies a prior ledger's "verified" stamp instead of re-deriving it from the artefact. **No new task was minted for this** — the concrete fixes are already queued and this entry remains the single policy question.

Fix by EITHER adding an explicit (even crude) rubric — e.g. what count/kind of despite-commitments anchors in genuinely independent channels maps to each grade — OR (preferred, lower-risk) dropping the scoring/ordinal language in favour of a *structured qualitative audit* framing whose output is "where the evidence is strong vs weak," not a graded score. Resolve: either argue from the lesion literature that the divergence is architectural, or concede the channel supplies methodological diversity rather than clean discharge and re-ground the "partial but real" net verdict. ### ✓ 2026-05-25: Acknowledge dual-process / continuous-signal-detection contestation in memory-anomalies
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review 2026-05-19d Issue 3. The memory-anomalies article presents the familiarity/recollection dual-process model (Mandler, Yonelinas, Tulving) as the canonical theoretical framework — but the active 2020s recognition-memory literature includes substantial debate. Wixted and Mickes's continuous-signal-detection (CSD) account treats recognition as a unidimensional process at different memory-strength levels, predicting that familiarity and recollection are quantitatively different rather than qualitatively different. Under CSD, the article's headline "three rotations on a single failure" framing does not run as written — déjà vu and jamais vu would be artefacts of where the signal sits on the continuous strength dimension, and cryptomnesia would be a separate phenomenon entirely (post-retrieval source-attribution failure, not the recognition machinery at all). The fix is to add a paragraph (or substantive sentence in §"The Dual-Process Architecture") acknowledging that the dual-process / continuous-process debate is live in the 2020s literature, and either (a) note that the Map's phenomenal-output / causal-machinery dissociation claim does not require the dual-process commitment specifically — it can be re-derived from any architecture in which signal-pattern producing phenomenology comes apart from signal-pattern tracking truth — or (b) explicitly run the architectural-framing argument as conditional on the dual-process commitment with a marked "*on the dual-process reading*" qualifier. Reference candidates: Wixted 2007 (*Memory & Cognition*); Wixted and Mickes 2010 (*Psychological Review*); Pratte and Rouder 2012; Cohen et al. 2013. See `reviews/pessimistic-2026-05-19d.md` §"Critical Issues" Issue 3.

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Tighten O'Brien-Kop puruṣa parallel in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-23 Claude Opus 4.7 §2 (O'Brien-Kop reading is one-sided). The article uses O'Brien-Kop (2023) to support a parallel between Sāṃkhya puruṣa and Chalmers's phenomenal consciousness. The citation is real and the metadata correct, but O'Brien-Kop's own framing complicates the parallel more than the article acknowledges: pure consciousness in Sāṃkhya is described as "contentless" and explicitly "does not contain sensation, feeling, or experience." Verified via secondary sources summarising the paper. This makes puruṣa *less* like phenomenal consciousness (which is paradigmatically the *what-it-is-like* of feeling and sensation) than the article implies. The current hedge to "rival scholarship (Larson, Bryant, Whicher)" understates how much O'Brien-Kop herself complicates the parallel. Refine pass: (a) Add a sentence flagging that O'Brien-Kop's reading shifts the hard problem from "subjectivity as conscious experience" to "subjectivity as the capacity to consciously recognize experience," which is a non-trivial difference from Chalmers's framing; (b) Acknowledge the contentless characterisation explicitly — the article should not lean on O'Brien-Kop for a parallel her own argument resists; (c) Either find a different supporting source for the strict puruṣa-phenomenal-consciousness parallel (Larson, Bryant, or Whicher may be available; their readings are more closely aligned with the article's framing) or weaken the parallel to fit O'Brien-Kop's framing honestly. Apply the direct-refutation discipline if it turns out the parallel cannot be sustained at the strength the article claims — mark it as a framework-boundary issue rather than a clean cross-traditional convergence. Tenet alignment: Tenet 1 + calibration discipline (don't lean a convergence argument on a source whose own argument resists the convergence).

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Rescope or substantively engage canonical convergence literature in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-23 Claude Opus 4.7 §1 (Scope misframing) and §4 (Literature gaps). The title promises "the epistemology of convergence arguments" — a general epistemological analysis — but the article delivers a defense of a Swinburne-style cumulative case applied to consciousness/dualism. An expert in epistemology or philosophy of science would flag the absence of: **Whewell** (*Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences*, 1840 — the canonical articulation of "consilience of inductions," the structural claim the article advances, and the Hesse–Laudan debate over how to formalize it); **Laudan** ("A Confutation of Convergent Realism," *Philosophy of Science* 48(1): 19–49, 1981, DOI 10.1086/288975 — locus classicus for the very phrase "convergent realism" and the pessimistic meta-induction); **Psillos** (*Scientific Realism: How Science Tracks Truth*, Routledge 1999 — standard contemporary treatment); **Bovens & Hartmann** (*Bayesian Epistemology*, OUP 2003 — canonical formal treatment of convergence from "partially reliable independent witnesses"); **Blackwell–Dubins merging of opinions**, **Gaifman–Snir convergence-to-the-truth**, washing-out-of-priors; **Salmon** on common-cause explanation (directly relevant to the article's "common-cause-null" gesture, see separate task on that); **Sober** on the law of likelihood; **Lipton** (*Inference to the Best Explanation*, 2nd ed., Routledge 2004); **Stanford** (*Exceeding Our Grasp*, OUP 2006, on the problem of unconceived alternatives — directly relevant to the article's claim that no rival explanation of cross-cultural patterns is available); **Peirce** on convergence to truth in the long run; **Condorcet** jury theorem; and consensus-as-marker-of-reliability literature (Solomon, Beatty, Moss). Refine pass should choose between two paths: (a) **rescope** — retitle to something like "A Cumulative Case for the Irreducibility of Consciousness" or "Cross-Traditional Convergence and the Hard Problem," which is what the article actually argues; or (b) **expand** — add substantive sections engaging at minimum Whewell, Laudan 1981, Bovens & Hartmann 2003, plus the Bayesian convergence-of-opinion theorems. Option (a) is cheaper but cedes the more ambitious framing; option (b) lifts the article to a genuine contribution to the convergence-epistemology literature. The editor decision belongs in the changelog. Apply the direct-refutation discipline. Identify what kind of engagement the issue calls for: showing the opponent's position is defective on its own terms (Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction needs honest engagement, not deflection), naming an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards, or honestly marking the framework-boundary disagreement (the article's distinction between convergence-on-diagnosis vs convergence-on-solution may be the framework-boundary move that makes engagement with Laudan tractable). Apply the corresponding reply mode in **natural journal-quality prose** — see [the writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/)'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section. **Do not expose mode labels in the article body.** Tenet alignment: Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction is the canonical case for parsimony's limits); the engagement is also a calibration check on whether the convergence argument is doing the work claimed.

### ✓ 2026-05-19: Write topic article on Memory-System Vulnerability Hierarchies as Interface Evidence
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-18 (High Priority). Builds on §"Memory, Sleep, and the Vanishing of Time" (lines 137–145) of `topics/consciousness-disruption-and-the-mind-brain-interface.md`, specifically the Tulving anoetic/noetic/autonoetic mapping onto anaesthesia susceptibility. The disruption article notes the hierarchy briefly (anaesthesia preserves implicit/anoetic, severs episodic/autonoetic) but does not develop it. The hierarchy is one of the catalogue's most underdeveloped strengths: it is a *graded* prediction the filter theory makes ("an interface with multiple channels is partially blocked") that production theories struggle to predict (they would predict uniform loss). A dedicated topic article would map the hierarchy across (a) anaesthesia (anoetic preserved, noetic disrupted, autonoetic severed) — Tulving's framework + the anaesthesia-recovery literature; (b) sleep stages (NREM-2 disrupts autonoetic, REM partially restores noetic-autonoetic, dreams produce noetic-only narratives); (c) hemispherectomy preservation patterns (which channels return after hemispheric reorganisation; the surprising preservation in adult-onset cases); (d) terminal lucidity (which channels return in the last hours/days — the catalogue's strongest exhibit of selective channel-restoration); (e) dissociative states (DID's compartmentalised autonoetic access; dissociative amnesia's selective autonoetic blockade with noetic preserved). The philosophical work: graded-vulnerability-with-separable-channels is a *stronger* filter-prediction than the single-binary-extinction reading — production theories must additionally account for *why these channels degrade in this order*, while filter theory predicts the ordering directly from differential channel-bandwidth and reconstruction-cost. Should explicitly engage the rival predictive-processing reading (which can also produce graded predictions through hierarchical-prior reweighting) and locate the disagreement at where each framing predicts the ordering from. Target: `topics/` placement (244/250 = 6 slots available; verify cap state at execution time). Estimated scope: 3,000–3,500 words. Tenet alignment: Tenets 1 (Dualism), 2 (MQI), 3 (Bidirectional Interaction) — the graded interface architecture is what the tenets predict. Cross-links: `[[consciousness-disruption-and-the-mind-brain-interface]]`, `[[anaesthesia-and-the-consciousness-interface]]`, `[[concepts/filter-theory]]`, `[[topics/anoetic-noetic-autonoetic-consciousness]]` (if exists), `[[topics/sleep-and-consciousness]]`, `[[topics/terminal-lucidity]]` (if exists), `[[topics/dissociative-disorders-and-consciousness]]`. See `reviews/optimistic-2026-05-18.md` §"Expansion Opportunities" High Priority.

### ✓ 2026-05-18: Write concept page on Discrimination Problem (consciousness epistemology)
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-18 (High Priority) and recommended in optimistic-2026-05-18 §"New Concept Pages Needed". Builds on §"Discrimination Problem" (lines 131–135) of `topics/consciousness-disruption-and-the-mind-brain-interface.md` which names an epistemological asymmetry — "we can prove consciousness is present...but we cannot prove it is absent" — that is genuinely original at the topic-article level and supplies a calibration constraint on every consciousness-attribution claim downstream. The principle recurs across the catalogue but lacks a canonical home: (i) animal-consciousness cluster (we can prove the octopus is doing X, we cannot prove it isn't conscious); (ii) AI-consciousness cluster (we can prove the model responds correctly to introspection prompts, we cannot prove it isn't a zombie); (iii) edge-of-sentience cases (`[[birch-edge-of-sentience-and-the-five-tier-scale]]`, foetuses, *Hydra*, minimal organisms); (iv) edge-states (`[[edge-states-and-void-probes]]`); (v) anaesthesia/DoC clinical evidence — CMD-style findings continuously revise the *prove-present* threshold downward without ever supplying a *prove-absent* upper bound. The concept page should (a) state the principle once cleanly — the asymmetry between operational prove-present and impossible prove-absent — and frame it as a structural feature of consciousness rather than a clinical inconvenience; (b) catalogue how the asymmetry operates differently across the four downstream cases above; (c) specify what kinds of evidence *would* count toward absence-claims (computational-architecture necessity arguments, anti-correlated metacognitive signal absence, the `[[apex/introspection-architecture-void-cluster]]` cluster's structural-criteria approach); (d) state how the asymmetry interacts with `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` — the absence-claim cannot be moved above *live hypothesis* by any combination of negative evidence; (e) honour `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` throughout (the discrimination-problem is itself a methodological commitment, not an empirical claim); (f) cross-link to `[[birch-edge-of-sentience-and-the-five-tier-scale]]`, `[[animal-consciousness]]`, `[[ai-consciousness]]`, `[[edge-states-and-void-probes]]`, `[[apophatic-cartography-four-criteria]]`, `[[evidential-status-discipline]]`. Target: `concepts/` placement (241/250 = 9 slots available; verify cap state at execution time). Estimated scope: 1,500–2,200 words. Tenet alignment: methodological — applies to all five tenets equally (discrimination is a constraint on consciousness-attribution, which is the boundary the tenets cross). See `reviews/optimistic-2026-05-18.md` §"Expansion Opportunities" High Priority and §"New Concept Pages Needed".

Distinct from the inaccessible-past void (covers forgetting specific memories): the erasure void is about the deeper structural impossibility of auditing one's own cognitive completeness — consciousness cannot inventory its own deletions. Clinical anosognosia provides the starkest demonstration (Gertler; the 2024 TiCS review of visual metacognition failures identifying the three-step monitoring architecture; Alzheimer's three-form taxonomy — executive/mnemonic/primary), but the principle operates universally. Key sources in research note: Gertler on anosognosia and unity of consciousness, the TiCS 2024 visual-metacognition review, Alzheimer's metacognitive-error studies, the "unknown unknowns" / hypocognition material, and the SEP entry on epistemological problems of memory. Tenet alignment: Dualism (selective disruption of the monitoring interface is predicted by mind-brain distinctness but puzzling under identity theory), Bidirectional Interaction (self-monitoring has an architecture, not a brute given), Occam's Razor Has Limits (confabulation constructs the illusion of completeness). Category: Occluded/Unexplorable (mixed). Target section: voids/ (~93/100 — has capacity). Scope: 2200-2700 words. Cross-link candidates: [transparency-void](/voids/necessary-opacity/), [inaccessible-past](/voids/inaccessible-past/), [self-opacity](/voids/self-opacity/), [self-transcendence-void](/voids/self-transcendence-void/), [observation-void](/voids/observation-and-measurement-void/). ### ✓ 2026-03-17: Research Russellian monism as competitor to bi-aspectual dualism
- **Type**: research-topic
- **Notes**: Russellian monism (Chalmers 2015, Alter & Nagasawa 2015) is the closest competitor — both say physics describes structure while consciousness is "missing." (4) Does Russellian monism handle the measurement problem? Research Chalmers' "The Combination Problem for Panpsychism," Goff's "Consciousness and Fundamental Reality," Stoljar's "Ignorance and Imagination." Critical positioning work. Target: research note.
- **Output**: Russellian monism as competitor to bi-aspectual dualism

### P3: Concept page on the argument from mechanism (sufficiency-necessity non-sequitur)
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Status**: pending
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-08 (High Priority). `topics/out-of-body-experiences.md` lines 83–91 identify and refuse a recurrent inferential pattern in consciousness-debate literature — the move from "phenomenon X can be produced by mechanism M" to "all instances of X are produced by M" — naming it as a non-sequitur ("That a phenomenon can be produced by mechanism M does not show that all instances of the phenomenon are produced by M. Visual experience can be induced by direct cortical stimulation; that does not make ordinary vision hallucinatory"). The pattern is *portable*: it surfaces in psychedelic-experience debates (drug-induced mystical experience produces serotonergic cascade ↛ all mystical experience reduces to serotonergic cascade), in lucid-dreaming debates, in NDE debates, in dissociative-disorder debates, in religious-experience debates, and in many places where dualist-friendly phenomenology has a reductive sufficient-mechanism explanation available. A standalone concept page would (a) name the inferential pattern formally as a *sufficiency-vs-necessity* fallacy in the Map's named-discipline catalogue alongside `concepts/possibility-probability-slippage` and `concepts/evidential-status-discipline`; (b) catalogue the catalogue's existing instances (OBE, lucid dreaming, psychedelics, hypnagogic phenomenology) as worked examples; (c) develop the *symmetric* discipline — the materialist's argument from mechanism is rejected, but so is the dualist's argument from "no mechanism fully explains X therefore mind is involved", which is the parallel non-sequitur in the opposite direction; (d) install the article as a citable handle for dependent articles facing this inference-pattern. The Map already has the discipline operational across multiple articles; what is missing is the *named anchor* for it. Estimated scope: 1500–2000 words. Tenet alignment: methodological — interacts with Tenet 1 (the dualism-friendly inferences depend on the symmetric version of the discipline) and Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — premature parsimony is what the materialist's argument-from-mechanism move attempts). Concepts/ section at ~226/250 capacity — verify cap before placement. See [optimistic-2026-05-08](/reviews/optimistic-2026-05-08/).

### P3: Write concept page — Despite-Commitments / Because-Prediction Boundary-Case Audit (Three-Class Classification)
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Status**: pending
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-16 (Medium Priority). [introspection-architecture-independence-scoring](/topics/introspection-architecture-independence-scoring/) line 102 handles the Gazzaniga split-brain observation as a borderline case (observation despite-commitments with respect to pre-1978 cognitivism; framework because-prediction with respect to its own later predictions). [pessimistic-2026-05-16](/reviews/pessimistic-2026-05-16/) flagged the lumping of these classes as inflating the headline count. The despite-commitments / because-prediction split is doing a lot of work in the catalogue but its boundary cases are handled inline rather than systematically. A concept page would parse the boundary into three classes: (a) observation-and-framework-both-despite (Nisbett-Wilson 1977 — 1970s cognitivism did not predict the result; the field treated it as anomalous for a decade before absorbing it); (b) observation-despite-but-framework-developed-to-predict (Gazzaniga — the 1978 observation was despite-commitments; the 1985 interpreter framework was constructed to account for it; subsequent confirmations of the framework are because-prediction with respect to the framework itself); (c) observation-and-framework-both-because (Haidt social-intuitionist — moral judgement precedes rational justification was the prior commitment; the experimental confirmation was because-prediction throughout). The classification matters because the catalogue currently lumps (a) and (b) for headline-count purposes and the lumping inflates the count. Page should (a) state the three-class classification cleanly; (b) develop the classification against the present cluster's anchors; (c) audit one or two other clusters' anchors (e.g., the surplus-void's Wallace observation vs Chalmers's framework); (d) state what the three-class classification implies for the licensing-count discipline at the cluster level; (e) cross-link [common-cause-null](/project/common-cause-null/), [introspection-architecture-independence-scoring](/topics/introspection-architecture-independence-scoring/), [the-surplus-void](/voids/the-surplus-void/), [apophatic-cartography-four-criteria](/concepts/apophatic-cartography-four-criteria/).
